Our $100M Seed to Build Open Infrastructure for Frontier AI | RadixArk Blog

May 5, 2026

# Our $100M Seed to Build Open Infrastructure for Frontier AI

Today, we are officially launching RadixArk with $100 million in Seed funding at a $400 million post-money valuation. The round was led by Accel and co-led by Spark Capital, with participation from NVentures, Salience Capital, A&E Investment, HOF Capital, Walden Catalyst, AMD, LDVP, WTT Fubon Family, MediaTek, Databricks and more.

## Our Mission: Making AI infra open and accessible

AI has moved quickly, but the infrastructure behind it has not yet been built the way it should be.

Frontier labs have some of the strongest internal systems in the world. But even there, infrastructure is often built under the pressure of delivering the next model, supporting the next architecture, or scaling the next workload. The system is often not designed from first principles to be the most reliable, efficient, and generally useful foundation for the broader AI ecosystem.

Outside of these labs, the problem is even more painful. Every company building AI is forced to rebuild the same foundations again and again: inference engines, RL frameworks, orchestration layers, evaluation pipelines, and production tooling. As models, hardware platforms, and use cases become more diverse, this duplication becomes increasingly expensive for everyone.

RadixArk exists to change this. We believe AI infrastructure should be built once, built deeply, and shared broadly. The best systems should not remain locked inside a few organizations. They should be open, reliable, production-ready, and improved with the community.

## Rooted in Open Source: SGLang and Miles

Our work starts from two open-source foundations: SGLang for inference and Miles for reinforcement learning and post-training.

- SGLang (Inference Engine): Since its creation in 2023, SGLang has quickly become a de-facto open-source standard for inference. Today, it powers trillions of tokens daily for industry leaders such as Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Oracle, AMD, LinkedIn, xAI, Thinking Machines Lab, humans&, and others.
- Miles (RL Framework): Our open-source framework for large-scale training serves as the second foundation of RadixArk, powering reinforcement learning at scale. Although Miles was introduced only recently, it has already been adopted by industry teams for large-scale MoE training, with a focus on efficiency and stability.

We come from the open-source community, and we intend to keep building with it. We will use this capital to grow SGLang and Miles, support new model architectures and hardware platforms, and build managed infrastructure for teams developing AI at scale. In an era where AI makes ordinary productivity cheaper, the rare work is still the same: patient refinement, independent thinking, and an uncompromising pursuit of correctness. We want this to be the culture of RadixArk: focused, humble, fearless, and meticulous about the details that make infrastructure truly work.

RadixArk is an infrastructure-first company. We care about performance, correctness, reliability, hardware efficiency, and long-term system design. To us, infrastructure engineering is not a support function. It is a core creative discipline that determines how fast models can improve, how efficiently they can run, and how widely frontier AI can be built.

The next generation of AI should not be limited by access to private infrastructure. More builders should be able to own their models, their systems, and their future.

That is what RadixArk is here to build. If this mission resonates with you, and if you believe AI infrastructure should be open, deeply engineered, and built for everyone pushing the frontier, we hope you will consider joining us.

The RadixArk Team

# 芯片三巨头，投了一位九江女生

###### 2026年11月25日 08:00 21世纪商业评论 鄢子为,谢之迎 

开源起家，中立突围。

 

撰文丨鄢子为 谢之迎 编辑丨鄢子为

美国科技大佬，集体投了一位九江女生。

11月中旬，RadixArk发布其首个开源大模型DaisyRose-27B。RadixArk是家AI基础设施初创公司，年中已完成1亿美元种子轮融资，投后估值约28亿元人民币。

投资人阵容豪华，英伟达NVentures、AMD、联发科三家芯片巨头罕见同框，还有英特尔CEO陈立武、博通CEO陈福阳等以个人身份入场。

RadixArk成立于2025年7月。联合创始人兼CEO盛颖，90后，江西九江人，本科毕业于上海交通大学ACM班，在斯坦福拿到博士学位。

其核心产品SGLang，是个“跑模型”的加速器，负责又快又省地把活儿派给GPU干，再把结果收回来。

盛颖不训练模型、不卖GPU，站在算力、模型与应用之间，致力于造一个工具箱，让用户按需取用。

免费获客

盛颖对开源的执念，要从自身经历说起。

小时候，她想学编程，身边资源匮乏，只能上网找别人留下的帖子、博客和在线题库。“我是被互联网上不知道在世界哪里的人给raise（养）起来的。”

念博士时，她把研究方向转向大模型推理。她做了S-LoRA，让一块GPU同时服务数千个微调模型；还做了公平调度算法VTC，研究多个用户怎么公平地分享算力。

用她的话说，SGLang是把此前那些局部研究“集大成为一体”的作品。

2023年，SGLang起步于加州大学伯克利分校的实验室。

盛颖以核心发起人的身份参与其中，一年后，与Lianmin Zheng等人发表了《SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs》论文。

“我希望把它做成一个可以被大规模广泛使用的、部署就绪的推理引擎。”盛颖表示。

2024年10月，盛颖加入马斯克旗下的xAI，为Grok搭建推理系统。

xAI前高管Igor Babuschkin说，SGLang是xAI基础设施的关键部分，让团队能比用其他方案更快、更高效地运行大模型。

去年夏天，在入职刚满十个月，第一笔股权马上就能兑现的关口，盛颖选择从xAI离开，和朱邦华一起创立公司。

Radix取自核心技术RadixAttention，Ark意为方舟。

盛颖（右）与联合创始人朱邦华在 RadixArk 门前

SGLang靠“免费”获得了大量用户。

截至2026年，SGLang部署在全球超过40万张GPU上，每天在生产环境中生成数万亿token。用户名单包括谷歌、微软、英伟达、AMD、xAI、甲骨文、LinkedIn等头部科技公司。

比用户量更关键的，是SGLang的“Day-0适配”能力。

SGLang 开源仓库

每一次主流模型架构发生大变化，SGLang都能在模型发布当天完成支持。DeepSeek新版本、MiMo-V2-Flash、Nemotron系列刚落地，SGLang就已经能跑。

有相关人士评价，SGLang的Day-0不是“等模型发布再适配”，而是提前介入的联合调优。

这项能力背后，是工程团队对每一代模型架构的持续拆解和预判。

免费开源让它拿到了规模，规模又反过来变成了数据、场景和工程判断力。

打包工具

盛颖做的是AI基础设施层的生意。

她表示，成立RadixArk，是想好好地做一家infra-first（基础设施优先）的公司。

基础设施团队，长期被低估，总得做支持类任务，比如帮研究者把实验跑起来、帮产品端提升服务水平。

盛颖不这么看。她觉得，infra不是支持性角色，infra本身就是产品，具有美感。

眼下，她先啃两块：推理和强化学习。她认为，这是大模型生产流程中“最靠近用户的两个末端步骤”。

推理引擎让模型跑得更快，强化学习则能让模型变得更好用，适配特定场景。

具体来看，SGLang可以让模型回答问题时不把算过的内容反复计算，让硬件更快、更高效地跑起来。Miles能让模型收到奖励信号，越训练越符合实际需求。

Miles是RadixArk自己开源的项目，但SGLang是盛颖等人在LMSYS（一个非营利组织）做出来的社区产品，不归RadixArk私有，RadixArk是这个工具的主要开发者和运营方。

“公司的命脉不在（SGLang）这里。”盛颖说得很干脆。

她的生意经是：工具免费，收运行和维护的钱。

盛颖把客户分为四层：最底层是数据中心、云厂商，“我们想帮他们销售GPU”；第二层是推理服务商；第三层是训练、部署大模型的AI公司；最上面是想用AI改造业务的传统大企业。

中立，是盛颖手里的一张王牌。

RadixArk种子轮的股东名单里，大佬云集。英伟达、AMD、联发科等芯片企业在市场上针锋相对，却都押注了盛颖。

项目落地加速。

7月，RadixArk跟谷歌云合作，把SGLang的整套功能搬上TPU，目的是让新开源模型在TPU上也能跑，做到Day-0支持。

AMD这边，团队联合DigitalOcean，让DeepSeek V4 Pro的单卡速度超过每秒3500个token，整体吞吐量增长约10倍。

群敌在侧

RadixArk处在创业早期阶段，尚未公开收入、客户数量和产品定价。

开源产品商业化，有一道难题。技术越好用，大厂越倾向于自己部署。谷歌、微软等企业不缺工程师和算力，付费托管的动力不足。

竞争也在逼近。盛颖最直接的对手是vLLM。

vLLM团队创立的Inferact，2026年初拿到1.5亿美元融资。

有意思的是，vLLM奠基论文PagedAttention，作者名单里也有盛颖。她解释，自己当年“被合并进了vLLM那个项目”。

两家各有侧重：SGLang更早发力大规模集群部署，vLLM则长于长尾模型适配。路线趋同，双方形成互补。

再往外看，是直接卖推理服务的平台，比如Baseten、Fireworks AI。

AI推理需求爆发，两家估值大涨。完成最新一轮融资后，Baseten估值一举冲上130亿美元，Fireworks AI估值也飙升至175亿美元。

这两家也在用SGLang。在盛颖看来，这个游戏里没有输家：推理公司层出不穷，却没有谁因竞争而萎缩；AI正从训练转向推理，到了需要盈利和兑现的时候，市场还在变大。

面向 LLM 与多模态模型的高性能推理框架

还有一重挑战来自内部。

在xAI，盛颖目睹了一家小企业快速长成大公司时的阵痛。

“scale（规模化）上去之后，文化就很脆弱了。”如今作为决策者，她表示，“做好了是团队的功劳，做坏了是我的责任。”

拿到融资只是开始，RadixArk能走多远，取决于盛颖未来交出的账本。

（记者何己派对本文亦有贡献）

RadixArk is a deep-tech company focused on developing large-scale infrastructure systems for AI training and inference. The firm spun out of SGLang, a popular open-source project from a UC Berkeley lab that helps accelerate the inference stage of AI models to reduce computing costs and improve performance. RadixArk was co-founded by CEO Ying Sheng, a former engineer at xAI and research scientist at Databricks. The company recently achieved a valuation of approximately $400 million, with funding from backers including venture capital firm Accel and angel investors such as Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan.

The company's mission is to make frontier-level AI infrastructure open and accessible to the entire AI community, which includes individual developers, research labs, startups, and large enterprises. RadixArk operates on an open-core business model. It continues to develop and support the open-source SGLang engine for model inference while building proprietary commercial offerings. Its product suite includes managed infrastructure and production-grade tooling for model inference and post-training. A key offering is 'Miles,' an open-source framework designed for large-scale reinforcement learning (RL) and post-training. Revenue is generated through managed hosting services and other commercial products built on top of its open-source foundations.

RadixArk aims to solve the problem of duplicated effort and siloed knowledge in AI infrastructure, where many companies rebuild similar systems from scratch. By providing robust, open, and scalable systems, the company enables the AI community to train, deploy, and operate advanced models more efficiently and affordably. The team consists of engineers with experience shipping production AI systems at companies like xAI and contributing to infrastructure that powers leading AI labs.

Nvidia, AMD back $100M round for AI tooling startup RadixArk - SiliconANGLE

 UPDATED 16:28 EDT / MAY 05 2026 

### Nvidia, AMD back $100M round for AI tooling startup RadixArk

 by Maria Deutscher 

RadixArk Inc., a startup that provides tools for artificial intelligence developers, has raised $100 million from a group of high-profile backers.

Accel led the seed round with Spark Capital. They were joined by Nvidia Corp.’s NVentures fund, Advanced Micro Devices Inc., Databricks Inc., Broadcom Inc. Chief Executive Hock Tan and others. The Wall Street Journal reported today that RadixArk is now worth $400 million.

The company is building commercial AI development tools based on two open-source projects called SGLang and Miles. Members of the RadixArk team helped develop the former technology prior to the company’s launch. Miles was open-sourced by RadixArk last November.

Software teams can use Miles to streamline reinforcement learning projects. Reinforcement learning is an AI training method that is commonly used to develop large language models. Miles can compress LLMs with one trillion parameters into a format that fits in the memory of a single high-end graphics card, which significantly reduces training costs.

The software also streamlines AI projects in other ways. It includes a so-called asynchronous co-evolutionary framework, MrlX, that can train multiple AI agents at the same time by placing them in the same simulated environment. That arrangement enables the agents to hone their reasoning capabilities by learning from one another.

After developers train an AI with Miles, they can use SGLang to perform inference. The latter project provides building blocks for building inference environments. According to RadixArk, SGLang powers AI clusters that contain more than 400,000 graphics cards in aggregate.

An LLM’s attention mechanism, a module that it uses to interpret user instructions, generates a significant amount of temporary data while processing prompts. That information is stored in a data structure called a KV cache. LLMs usually clear the KV cache after every prompt.

SGLang enables LLMs to reuse some KV cache data across prompts. That avoids the need to generate all the data from scratch after every request, which lowers the associated infrastructure overhead. Furthermore, SGLang speeds up prompt response times in the process. 

The tool’s KV cache reuse feature is complemented by several other performance optimizations. SGLang uses a method called speculative decoding to offload some tasks from an application’s LLM to a lighter, less hardware-intensive model. Additionally, the tool can spread the calculations involved in processing a prompt across chips with different architectures. That approach can significantly boost model performance in some cases. 

The commercial products that RadixArk plans to build using Miles and SGLang will include ”managed infrastructure and tooling.” According to the Journal, the offerings will enable customers to host AI models in the cloud. RadixArk also plans to enhance the open-source versions of SGLang and Miles.

Sysdig Raises $350M, Rides Cloud Security Wave - SDxCentral

# Sysdig Raises $350M, Rides Cloud Security Wave

 “The cloud security market has taken off and this is the time to expand capacity in every aspect of our business," CEO Suresh Vasudevan said. 

December 15, 2021

By
: Nancy Liu 

 Have your say 

Container and cloud security unicorn Sysdig today scored $350 million in a Series G funding round led by Permira. The cash infusion brings the total raised to $744 million and pushes the vendor's valuation to $2.5 billion.

“We took funding now because the cloud security market has taken off and this is the time to expand capacity in every aspect of our business, and we didn’t want capital to be a prohibitor,” Sysdig CEO Suresh Vasudevan told SDxCentral in an email.

Sysdig offers security and performance monitoring services tailored toward cloud-native applications. Today's funding round will enable the company to accelerate the expansion of these services into new markets, increase its headcount and customer base, and invest in research and development, Vasudevan said.

Sysdig’s customer base has grown 140% year over year to nearly 700 customers, and its average annual recurring revenue now tops more than $875,000 across its 50 largest customers, the vendor claims.

The company has also doubled its headcount over the past year and “plans to do it again with an eye on accelerating growth in Europe, Middle East, Asia Pacific, and South America,” Vasudevan wrote. 

Sysdig expanded its software-as-a-service (SaaS) hosting locations from nine to 16 over the same period and expects to bring more locations online in the near future. 

 Sysdig Extends Partnerships with Top Cloud Providers 

On top of the go-to-market build out, Sysdig also plans to deepen its partnerships with the major cloud providers including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and IBM Cloud.

Sysdig acquired Apolicy in August, which enabled the vendor to shift security further left by integrating Apolicy’s infrastructure as code (IaC) technology into its platform to better secure DevOps workflows. Not long after, the company launched guided remediation for IaC manifests and an out-of-the-box integration with GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, and BitBucket. 

Sysdig plans to make the ability to enforce compliance and governance via policy as code and its guided remediation functionality available early next year, Vasudevan said.

Sysdig also added cloud configuration risk management and cloud infrastructure entitlements management (CIEM) earlier this year. “Looking ahead, we will be extending these capabilities to all of the major cloud providers,” Vasudevan said. 

 Sysdig Open Source Platforms Gain Momentum 

Founded in 2013, Sysdig started with two open source projects as its foundation: the threat detection engine for container and cloud called Falco and its own platform for incident responses using deep data and context. 

The projects thrived, as Falco downloads increased to 37 million, up 335% since it became an incubating project in the cloud-native computing foundation (CNCF) in early 2020, Sysdig claims.

Those open source projects helped Sysdig drive the standards for cloud security, Vasudevan said. “Together, Sysdig and Falco have become industry standards for modern runtime security spanning threat and anomaly detection and incident response in containers and cloud,” he wrote in a blog post.

Despite enjoying rapid growth and another strong funding round, Sysdig doesn't plan to go public anytime soon, Vasudevan said. “Our belief is that going public in the short-term would take away from our focus on scaling and building the next great security company,” he added.

Security firm Sysdig raises $350 million in latest funding led by Permira

# Security firm Sysdig raises $350 million in latest funding led by Permira

 Krystal Hu December 15, 2021 2 min read

By Krystal Hu 

(Reuters) - Cloud security startup Sysdig has raised $350 million in its latest funding round from investors led by the growth fund of private equity firm Permira, the company said late on Tuesday. 

The fast-growing security vendor has doubled its valuation to $2.5 billion since its last private fund raising in April, as more enterprises continue to transition to cloud applications and demand more comprehensive security solutions. 

The company also said it has hired Karen Walker from PagerDuty as its chief financial officer, as it eyes an eventual path to the public market. 

"It's become clear to us that we want to be ready to go public and then we can make the choice on when is the right time," said Suresh Vasudevan, chief executive at Sysdig. 

Based in San Francisco, Sysdig provides unified interface to detect real-time threats and offers one-click remediation to eliminate security blind spots throughout the development and production cycle. It now serves nearly 700 enterprise customers, including Goldman Sachs and SAP. 

The company did not disclose its revenue, but said its customer base has more than doubled in the past year, and it has seen higher spending from existing customers as they adopt more cloud applications. More than half of its revenue comes from the U.S. market. 

The eight-year-old company plans to use the funding to expand its footprint in regions including the Middle East and Asia, with its global headcount doubling in 2022. 

"The global expansion of cloud deployments by our customers in the pandemic means that the market for securing those applications is growing extremely rapidly," said Vasudevan. 

Founded in 2013, Sysdig competes with Palo Alto Networks and Datadog. It has raised $744 million in total funding, counting Accel and Bain Capital Ventures as its backers. 

Alex Melamud, principal at Permira who led the investment, will join the board of Sysdig. 

(This story corrects the investor's title at Permira) 

(Reporting by Krystal Hu in New York; Editing by Christian Schmollinger)

# VA Linux Systems Secures $25m in Equity Funding

 CBR Staff Writer June 21, 1999 

 VA Linux Systems has won $25m in private equity funding in a second round of financing. Companies participating in the round include the Capital Research Group, WR Hambrecht & Co, Intel Corp, IDG Ventures, Lehman Brothers, Sequoia Capital, SGI, Sumitomo Corp and Presidio Venture Partners. Sunnyvale, California-based VA supplies Linux computer systems, support and internet services. Along with the funding, the company has announced the opening of two international offices in Toronto, Canada. Finally, to demonstrate its ongoing commitment to the open source and free software communities that develop the Linux operating system, VA has announced that it will sponsor Linux Demo Day. This volunteer project, run by corporate sponsors and Linux users groups (LUGs), aims to hold an international demonstration of Linux during the week of September 12-18, 1999.
